Beaten
BEE-tun
v. (past part.) / adj.
From Old English beatan, to strike. Webster 1828 gives, among the senses of BEATEN, hammered; formed by beating, and worn by treading, as a beaten path. Scripture uses both: the sanctuary’s holiest furniture was beaten work, and the servants and apostles of God were beaten men.

Biblical Definition

Beaten runs through Scripture along two lines that meet at the cross. The first is craftsmanship. The cherubim over the mercy seat were not cast or joined: of beaten work shalt thou make them, in the two ends of the mercy seat (Exodus 25:18), hammered out of the same piece as the lid. The candlestick likewise was of beaten gold… according unto the pattern which the LORD had shewed Moses (Numbers 8:4). And the light in the holy place burned on pure oil olive beaten for the light (Exodus 27:20) — oil pressed by hand from the first crushing of the fruit, the costliest and clearest grade. Every visible glory of the sanctuary was made by hammering and crushing. The second line is suffering. That servant, which knew his lord’s will, and prepared not himself… shall be beaten with many stripes (Luke 12:47), a warning of degrees in judgment. Paul counts his beatings among his credentials: Thrice was I beaten with rods (2 Corinthians 11:25), and at Philippi, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans (Acts 16:37). Isaiah’s Servant was beaten before either apostle was, and the gold of the sanctuary was always a picture of it.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 lists for BEATEN: hammered, formed by beating; worn by use or by treading, as a beaten road; and, figuratively, worn out or exhausted. The first sense is the sanctuary’s, the second is the proverb’s, and Scripture uses both.

expand to see more

BEATEN, pp. — Struck; dashed against; pounded; conquered; worn by treading.

Hammered; formed by beating; as beaten gold, beaten work — the technical term for metal shaped by the hammer rather than cast in a mould.

Made smooth or hard by treading; as a beaten path, a beaten track.

BEATEN OIL — oil obtained by pounding olives in a mortar rather than by pressing them in the mill; the purest sort, appointed for the lamp (Exodus 27:20).

Webster’s technical distinction matters: a cast image is poured into a shape by another’s design, but beaten work is drawn out of solid metal by long, patient blows.

Key Scripture

Exodus 25:18 — "And thou shalt make two cherubims of gold, of beaten work shalt thou make them, in the two ends of the mercy seat."

Numbers 8:4 — "And this work of the candlestick was of beaten gold, unto the shaft thereof, unto the flowers thereof, was beaten work: according unto the pattern which the LORD had shewed Moses, so he made the candlestick."

Exodus 37:7 — "And he made two cherubims of gold, beaten out of one piece made he them, on the two ends of the mercy seat;"

Luke 12:47 — "And that servant, which knew his lord’s will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes."

2 Corinthians 11:25 — "Thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I have been in the deep;"

Modern Corruption

Luke 12:47 teaches degrees of punishment in hell, and it is quietly dropped by two opposite parties — those who deny hell altogether, and those who preach it so flatly that Scripture’s own distinctions disappear.

expand to see more

Our Lord says the servant who knew his lord’s will and did it not shall be beaten with many stripes, and the one who knew not and did commit things worthy of stripes shall be beaten with few. The passage closes, unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required. The Reformed tradition has always taught degrees of punishment on the strength of this and of Matthew 11:22 about Tyre and Sidon, and it is a doctrine with a sharp edge for the churched. Sitting under faithful preaching is not a neutral condition. It raises the account. The man who has heard the gospel plainly for thirty years and never bowed is not in the position of the man who has never heard it, and he is not in a better one.

The sanctuary line of the word yields the other lesson, and it is a comfort rather than a warning. Everything that gave light or covered the mercy seat was made by beating: the cherubim hammered out of the same gold as the lid they overshadowed, the candlestick beaten from shaft to flower, the oil pounded from the olive. Nothing in the holy place was cast quickly in a mould. God’s ordinary method with what He intends to make beautiful and useful is long, repeated pressure, and Scripture says so plainly enough that no believer should read his afflictions as evidence of neglect. The trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew miqshah (H4749), beaten work, hammered out of one piece; kathith (H3795), beaten or pounded, of the oil; Greek dero (G1194), to flay or beat, and rhabdizo (G4463), to beat with rods.

expand to see more

Hebrew miqshah (H4749) — beaten work, of one piece; the cherubim and the candlestick (Exodus 25:18; Numbers 8:4).

Hebrew kathith (H3795) — beaten, pounded; of the pure olive oil for the lamp (Exodus 27:20).

Greek dero (G1194) — to flay, to beat; beaten with many stripes (Luke 12:47).

Greek rhabdizo (G4463) — to beat with rods; the Roman punishment Paul suffered thrice (2 Corinthians 11:25; Acts 16:22).

Greek plege (G4127) — a stripe, a blow; the noun behind many stripes and few stripes.

Usage

"Of beaten work shalt thou make them (Exodus 25:18) — the cherubim hammered from the mercy seat’s own gold."

"Pure oil olive beaten for the light (Exodus 27:20) — the crushed first pressing appointed for the lamp."

"Shall be beaten with many stripes (Luke 12:47) — degrees of punishment, taught by Christ."
